subject: computer-science
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What are the four stages of the program development life cycle in the correct order?
questions.explain: The program development life cycle runs analysis first, then design, then coding, and finally testing.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of the analysis stage of the program development life cycle?
options: Understanding and identifying the requirements of the problem
Writing the program code in a chosen language
Removing all logic and syntax errors
questions.explain: Analysis investigates the problem and establishes what the solution must do before any design or coding.

questions.q: Decomposition breaks a problem down into which three key components?
questions.explain: Decomposition describes a problem in terms of its inputs, the processes performed on them, and the outputs.

questions.q: What does a structure diagram represent?
options: A top-down, hierarchical breakdown of a system into sub-tasks
The step-by-step flow of control through an algorithm
The values of variables as an algorithm executes
The physical connections between hardware devices
questions.explain: A structure diagram shows top-down design by splitting a system into progressively smaller sub-tasks.

questions.q: Which tool is used to show the top-down design of a solution?
questions.explain: A structure diagram displays top-down design as a hierarchy of sub-problems.

questions.q: In Cambridge pseudocode, which symbol is used for assignment?
questions.explain: Cambridge pseudocode uses the left arrow ← to assign a value to a variable.

questions.q: Which flowchart symbol represents a decision?
questions.explain: A diamond represents a decision, where the flow branches based on a condition.

questions.q: What does a parallelogram symbol represent in a flowchart?
options: The start or stop of the algorithm
questions.explain: The parallelogram is used for input and output operations in a flowchart.

questions.q: How many times does the loop body run in: FOR Count ← 1 TO 5 ... NEXT Count?
questions.explain: A FOR loop from 1 to 5 inclusive executes its body five times.

questions.q: Which statement about a REPEAT ... UNTIL loop is correct?
options: Its body always runs at least once because the condition is tested at the end
Its body may never run because the condition is tested at the start
It always repeats exactly the number of times stated
It cannot contain any other statements inside it
questions.explain: REPEAT ... UNTIL is a post-condition loop, so the body executes before the condition is first checked.

questions.q: After this code, what value is stored in Count? Count ← 0  FOR i ← 1 TO 4  Count ← Count + i  NEXT i
questions.explain: The loop adds 1 + 2 + 3 + 4, giving a final total of 10.

questions.q: A binary search can only be used on a list that is:
questions.explain: Binary search relies on the data being ordered so it can discard half the list at each step.

questions.q: Why is a binary search usually faster than a linear search on a large sorted list?
options: It halves the number of items still to be searched at each step
It checks every item once in a fixed order
It does not need the data to be in order
It sorts the list again before each comparison
questions.explain: By comparing with the middle item, binary search discards half the remaining items each time.

questions.q: In a bubble sort, which items are compared with each other?
options: The first and last items only
An item and the middle item
questions.explain: A bubble sort repeatedly compares adjacent items and swaps them if they are in the wrong order.

questions.q: What is the maximum number of passes a bubble sort needs to sort a list of 6 items?
questions.explain: A bubble sort of n items needs at most n − 1 passes, so 6 items need at most 5.

questions.q: Which statement best describes a linear search?
options: Each item is checked in turn until the target is found or the list ends
The middle item is checked and half the list discarded
Adjacent items are compared and swapped
The list is split until each part has one item
questions.explain: A linear search inspects items one after another from the start until it finds the value or reaches the end.

questions.q: Which validation check ensures a value lies between a stated lower and upper limit?
questions.explain: A range check confirms that data falls within a defined minimum and maximum.

questions.q: What is the difference between validation and verification?
options: Validation checks data is reasonable; verification checks data was entered correctly
Validation checks data was entered correctly; verification checks data is reasonable
Both check that data is spelled correctly
Both check that hardware is working
questions.explain: Validation tests whether data is sensible/allowed, while verification checks it matches the source, e.g. by double entry.

questions.q: Which set correctly lists categories of test data used to test a program?
options: Normal, abnormal, extreme and boundary data
Fast, slow, medium and mixed data
questions.explain: Programs are tested with normal, abnormal (erroneous), extreme and boundary data to check all cases.

questions.q: A field accepts whole numbers from 1 to 100 inclusive. Which value is an example of boundary data?
questions.explain: Boundary data lies on the edge of the accepted range, so 100 (the upper limit) is a boundary value.

specSource: Cambridge IGCSE Computer Science (0478) syllabus; Algorithm Design & Problem Solving
